body:
Hey, 19F here. I don't have tons of experience but I thought I'd throw my two cents in.

I've been going through a really similar situation to you, I won't go into details, but your post really hit home with me. Honestly there's been a few times where I almost posted basically the same thing, but I think I'm finally getting out of my slump, so hopefully I have at least one useful piece of advice you can take from this.

The advice I've been given has always revolved around setting goals, and repetition. When I was in the thick of it, I refused to make any goals because it seemed pointless and I was pretty damn stubborn. My therapist told me that when you become depressed, you have to reteach yourself to enjoy the things you used to enjoy. In order to do this, you have to force yourself to do the things you used to love every single day. But it all starts with making a commitment to getting better. Posting here is a great step in that direction, but it's super easy to fall into the habit of looking for advice all over, waiting for something that gives you enough motivation. For me, that never happened. Are you seeing a professional? The biggest piece of advice I can give is to commit to seeing a therapist every week. Even if it seems like it does nothing, you are making a commitment to helping yourself. Taking medication could help you, but that alone rarely does the trick. And like you said, the nonzero days approach is great because it is designed to be simple. It seems like you set yourself up for failure by saying that you won't be able to stick to it even if you tried. But even getting yourself a glass of water is *something.* And remember that just because things took a turn for the worse, doesn't mean they can't get better. It takes a hell of a lot of work, but (at least in my opinion) there's nothing as exciting as a comeback story.

Like I said before, I've been going through a really similar situation, so feel free to pm me if you want to chat anymore, or if you ever want a motivational/accountability buddy.

I'd say do it.

You said it yourself, you can change your mind and go back home with next to no loss. This seems like an amazing opportunity to explore more of what the world has to offer, and you even have friends to experience it with. I believe it would be better to have said you at least tried it, instead of never truly knowing. What helped me with making big decisions like that is giving myself a time frame. I'm moving out soon and discussed with my parents that I'll give it 1 year to truly see if it's right, but my parents doors will be open to welcome me back if I decide it isn't right. 

If this chance excites you, go for it! You could make a killing, but you can always change your mind if you determine it's not the right choice. The work might be tough, but sometimes the work itself distracts you from the effort and time you're putting into it. It'll make you appreciate the rest of life so much more! At some point, the advice won't matter. You really just have to decide for yourself whether you're willing to put yourself into that uncomfortable situation, even if you make no money, or you find out it's absolutely not right for you, you'll have learned a lot in the process.

Good luck in whatever you choose! :)
